label: NA-01
title: Floating-point arithmetic, conditioning, and error propagation
description:
Reuse, without reissuing, the published definitions of the standard relative floating-point model and unit roundoff, γ_n accumulation, dot-product error, conditioning, backward stability, and residual-to-forward-error bounds. Organize their interface as exact problem → computed quantity → backward perturbation → condition-amplified forward error. State the normal-range premise for each rounded operation and keep overflow, underflow, subnormals, invalid operations, cancellation, and exceptional results visible. Proposed interfaces are a page-level error taxonomy and, only if a new item is needed, a proved triangle-inequality error ledger; the existing local definitions remain canonical.

Proof route: Point to the published Linear Algebra contracts for every numerical inequality. For a new total-error lemma, insert intermediate targets and apply the norm triangle inequality; do not combine variances without centering and covariance/independence hypotheses. Examples and page prose must distinguish model sensitivity from algorithm instability.

Binding contract completion: Distinguish absolute and relative errors; relative formulas require nonzero denominators. Retain n u<1 for γ_n and normal-range/exact-zero operation premises. The total-error lemma specifies intermediate targets in one normed space.

label: NA-02
title: Finite-precision direct factorizations and least squares
description:
Add alg-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal with the Hermitian positive-definite recurrence d_j=a_jj−Σ_{k<j}|l_jk|², l_jj=√d_j>0, and l_ij=(a_ij−Σ_{k<j}l_ik conjugate(l_jk))/l_jj. Prove pivot admissibility and exact correctness. A rounded run may encounter a nonpositive computed pivot even for positive-definite input: return failure there, and state the backward theorem conditional on successful completion or prove a quantitative sufficient condition for success. The real four-operation rounding model supplies neither rounded square roots nor complex operations; add their explicit arithmetic models/results before using them. Add a computed-Cholesky backward-error theorem with explicit componentwise/normwise constants, and a Householder local-step lemma only under the published standard relative model and stated range conditions. If computed least-squares stability is promised, add a separate full-column-rank computed-solution theorem covering reflector formation, Q*b, triangular substitution, and the nearby (A,b) perturbation. Preserve the existing Householder theorem’s explicit A1 premise until that premise is proved and integrated with a fresh dependency/consumer review; it remains conditional here. Do not add a numerical-SVD algorithm: the direct packet has no read full-text algorithm/stability source.

Proof route: Derive each Cholesky pivot from the positive-definite Schur complement; bound every rounded sum, square root, and division; assemble the Hermitian residual A+E=Lhat Lhat*. For Householder QR, prove stable scaling and reflector construction, then the rank-one update perturbation, including the zero-vector case; aggregate local errors by exact orthogonality. For computed least squares, add the Q*b and triangular-solve residuals before applying the least-squares condition bound. Derive flop costs only under an explicit operation convention.

Binding contract completion: Cholesky loops j=1,…,n and i=j+1,…,n return L or the first invalid pivot/range status. A complex implementation names real component operations, conjugation and square-root rounding. Householder analysis uses exact orthogonal mathematical representatives, not a falsely exactly orthogonal stored matrix. Full-rank computed LS retains residual-dependent conditioning and successful triangular pivots.

title: Finite-precision direct factorizations and least squares — Examples
description: positive-definite 2×2 Cholesky recurrence and a computed residual; a full-rank least-squares problem comparing normal equations with reduced QR; an ill-conditioned design matrix showing why stability does not imply small forward error.

label: NA-03
title: Sparse matrix models and kernel costs
description:
Define a fixed CSR access model, including dimensions, row pointers, values, column indices, and duplicate/empty-row conventions; define CSR matrix–vector multiplication; prove storage O(s+m) and operation count O(m+s), where s counts stored entries. Only for a canonical representation with no duplicates or explicit zeros is s=nnz(A). For square patterns with at least one stored entry per row, state the O(s) specialization. Distinguish sparse matvec/vector-kernel costs from convergence and from sparse direct-factorization fill, which depends on the graph and ordering. Do not state a universal factorization cost from matrix dimension alone.

Proof route: Count stored values, column indices, row pointers, and loop iterations under the declared format. Treat algorithmic costs as arithmetic/storage counts, not runtime or memory-bandwidth claims. Use a concrete elimination graph to show fill without asserting a general fill bound.

Binding contract completion: CSR uses m,n≥0, s stored entries, r₀=0≤…≤r_m=s, 0≤c_k<n; duplicates are summed and explicit zeros count as stored entries. Set y_i=0, then for k=r_i,…,r_(i+1)−1 add v_k x_(c_k). Cost is O(m+s), storage O(m+s); use s, not mathematical nnz, until a canonical no-duplicates/no-zero format is imposed.

label: NA-04
title: Stationary iterations and relaxation
description:
Define a matrix splitting A=M−N and the stationary update x_{j+1}=M^-1Nx_j+M^-1b; supply Richardson, Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel, and SOR as exact algorithms with their admissible diagonal/pivot rules. State the all-start/all-right-hand-side convergence equivalence ρ(M^-1N)<1. Prove only the source-backed sufficient tests: strict diagonal dominance, or irreducible weak diagonal dominance with at least one strict row, for Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel; for symmetric A with positive diagonal, SOR converges for every start iff A is positive definite and 0<ω<2. Keep ordering assumptions on any optimal-ω formula.

Proof route: Reduce the error to G^j e_0; use Jordan form/spectral radius for the all-start equivalence and norm contraction only as a sufficient condition. Explicitly permit transient nonnormal growth and polynomial factors from defective dominant roots. Prove named matrix-class criteria separately from the general theorem.

Binding contract completion: Iteration sequences have arbitrary n≥1, nonsingular M and fixed ordering; executable runs take a budget and residual test. Jacobi uses D, GS D−L, SOR D−ωL for A=D−L−U; Richardson uses M=ω⁻¹I with ω≠0. A zero diagonal returns failure for Jacobi/GS/SOR. Prove weak irreducible dominance plus a strict row, not irreducibility alone.

label: NA-05
title: Krylov methods and Lanczos convergence
description:
Reuse the published exact-arithmetic Krylov, Arnoldi, GMRES, CG, MINRES, residual, grade, and termination contracts without copying their items. Add a separate sparse CSR cost proposition for m-step unrestarted Arnoldi/GMRES: O(m nnz(A)+m²n) arithmetic and O(mn) basis storage under the square nonempty-row pattern assumption, plus the small least-squares solve. Add an extremal Lanczos Ritz-value theorem for real symmetric A with λ₁>λ₂≥…≥λ_n, a unit starting vector with nonzero dominant component, and explicit starting-angle and spectral-gap factors. Do not imply computed finite-precision CG/Lanczos terminates in the exact grade.

Proof route: Count matvecs and orthogonalization separately. For Lanczos, combine the Ritz residual identity with Chebyshev polynomial approximation on the unwanted spectral interval; retain the start-angle denominator and gap in the bound. State ghost Ritz values/loss of orthogonality as finite-precision behavior, not as a contradiction to the exact theorem.

Binding contract completion: The m-step sparse bound requires 1≤m≤n and a specified orthogonalization strategy. Incremental Givens small-LS work O(m²) fits the O(m²n) term; solving every dense small LS afresh has a different cost. Happy breakdown returns the invariant-space solution; numerical near-breakdown has its own status. Lanczos Chebyshev bound separates the degenerate interval λ₂=λ_n and n=1; the starting angle/gap cannot be omitted.

label: NA-06
title: Preconditioner algorithms and residual metrics
description:
Reuse the published left/right/symmetric preconditioning maps, residual identities, SPD-preconditioned CG transformation, flexible-GMRES condition, and counterexample to universal improvement. Add a precisely defined zero-fill incomplete LU procedure for a fixed ordering and sparsity pattern: return either the factors or an explicit zero-pivot failure; prove its retained pattern and count storage/application work in terms of nnz(L)+nnz(U). Keep setup cost, application cost, and Krylov convergence separate. Do not claim ILU improves conditioning or iteration count for arbitrary A.

Proof route: Show algebraically that left and right preconditioning preserve the exact solution set but minimize different residuals. For the ILU procedure, specify the recurrence, stored positions, and failure branch, then count operations under the input graph. For variable right preconditioners, use the actual preconditioned-vector span in flexible GMRES; do not reuse fixed-preconditioner spectral claims.

Binding contract completion: ILU(0) fixes an ordering and pattern containing the diagonal, copies stored A, processes pivots in increasing order and drops every update outside that pattern; an absent/zero pivot returns failure before division. Factors are preconditioner maps only after invertibility is proved. Setup work depends on pattern intersections; triangular application/storage use stored factor entries.

label: NA-07
title: Multigrid methods and complexity
description:
Define fine/coarse spaces, prolongation P, restriction R, Galerkin operator A_H=RA_hP, smoothing step, two-grid error operator, and one stated V-cycle. Prove the Galerkin coarse correction is an A_h-orthogonal projector for SPD A_h under the stated transfer identities. Prove the two-grid contraction from smoothing and approximation inequalities with constants 0<α≤β uniform in mesh level; keep convergence separate from cycle work. State the recursion T(N)=cN+γT(N/2^d) with its three Master-theorem regimes. FMG order and AMG selection are separate conditional claims; no arbitrary algebraic coarsening is declared convergent.

Proof route: Derive the projector identity, then use the exact smoothing and approximation estimates to obtain the one-sided bound sqrt(1−α/β); for symmetric pre/post smoothing use the A_h-adjoint relation. Prove work by recursion-tree counting. A mesh-independent rate requires level-uniform α,β; a rediscretized operator is not identified with the Galerkin operator without an equality proof.

Binding contract completion: Specify SPD A_h, full-column-rank P, R=P*, and SPD A_H=P*A_hP. C=I−P A_H⁻¹P*A_h is the A_h-orthogonal error projector. Set D=diag(A_h)>0, require ||S e||_A²≤||e||_A²−α||A_h e||_(D⁻¹)² and inf_v ||e−Pv||_D²≤β||e||_A². The product is S C for post-smoothing after correction; the A-adjoint proves the corresponding pre-smoothing norm. The bound is sqrt(1−α/β). A finite hierarchy plus finite smoother counts defines a V-cycle; exact/coarse iterative solve is declared. Master recurrence includes base level and γ<,=,>2^d cases O(N), O(N log N), O(N^(log_(2^d)γ)).

label: NA-08
title: Randomized low-rank approximation
description:
Define the real Gaussian range finder for fixed A∈R^{m×n}, k≥2, p≥2, k+p≤min(m,n): draw Ω with iid N(0,1) entries, form Y=AΩ, compute an orthonormal basis Q for Ran(Y), and return QQ*A. Prove the expected spectral error bound E||A−QQ*A||₂ ≤ (1+√(k/(p−1)))σ_{k+1} + e√(k+p)/p (Σ_{j>k}σ_j²)^{1/2}. The expectation is over Ω and the theorem assumes exact arithmetic. Do not add SRFT embedding or a-posteriori estimator claims whose proofs were omitted by the read source.

Proof route: Establish the deterministic SVD-partition bound first; then supply local Gaussian pseudoinverse-moment, pseudoinverse-tail, spectral-norm, and concentration lemmas before taking expectations. Use independence of Ω₁,Ω₂ and local Eckart–Young for the optimal baseline. For a power scheme, prove its power inequality separately and insert QR orthonormalization between A and A* applications in any floating-point discussion.

Binding contract completion: Gaussian drawing is a probabilistic primitive; Q spans all of Ran(AΩ), even when its rank is below k+p. A rank-revealing exact basis routine handles rank loss deterministically. The returned projector has rank up to k+p, not necessarily k. Expected error uses the deterministic block bound and local Gaussian moment lemmas; tail/concentration are separately required only for a promised probability bound.

label: NA-09
title: Nonlinear equations and Newton methods
description:
Define fixed-point iteration, damped Newton and a finite-difference Jacobian variant with explicit input/output and stopping status. Prove local quadratic convergence of ordinary variable-Jacobian Newton only for F∈C³, DF invertible in a neighborhood of a root, and a sufficiently close initial point. Reuse the local frozen-Jacobian contraction only for its stated map; it is not ordinary Newton. No arbitrary-start or global convergence theorem is claimed.

Proof route: Taylor-expand F(x_j) at the root, use a uniform local inverse-Jacobian bound and a local invariant ball to derive ||e_{j+1}||≤C||e_j||², then prove the iterate remains in that ball. For line search, prove only the stated accepted-step decrease under its assumptions; distinguish convergence of the nonlinear solve from discretization accuracy.

Binding contract completion: Newton accepts x₀, residual norm/tolerance, budget and derivative/linear-solve oracle; singular Jacobian, inadmissible trial state and exhausted backtracking are failure statuses. Finite-difference increments are nonzero and samples must lie in the domain. No quadratic rate is transferred to damped, frozen or approximate-Jacobian variants without a separate perturbation theorem.

label: NA-10
title: Polynomial interpolation and remainder
description:
For distinct real nodes x₀,…,x_n in [a,b], define cardinal polynomials ℓ_j and I_nf=Σf(x_j)ℓ_j; prove I_nf is the unique degree-at-most-n interpolant. For f∈C^{n+1}[a,b], prove the pointwise Lagrange remainder at every non-node x. State the barycentric evaluation formula as an algebraically equivalent procedure, with its finite-precision conditioning kept separate. Do not infer uniform convergence without node and function-class bounds.

Proof route: Verify cardinal values for existence; the difference of two interpolants has n+1 roots, so polynomial root count gives uniqueness. For the remainder, use an auxiliary multiple of the node product and repeated Rolle. Add the local higher-order Rolle intermediate explicitly; source samples that state uniqueness as known do not discharge this proof.

Binding contract completion: Barycentric weights w_j=1/∏_(k≠j)(x_j−x_k); at an exact node return f(x_j), otherwise return (Σw_j f(x_j)/(x−x_j))/(Σw_j/(x−x_j)). Prove the denominator is nonzero in exact arithmetic. Rounded denominator/range failure is explicit. Higher-order Rolle handles distinct nodes; Hermite repeated nodes need the separate multiplicity lemma in NA-13.

title: Polynomial interpolation and remainder — Examples

label: NA-11
title: Polynomial approximation and Chebyshev interpolation
description:
Define the best degree-n uniform approximation error E_n(f) and the interpolation operator norm Λ_n=||I_n||_{C→C}. For Chebyshev-root or Chebyshev–Lobatto nodes, prove Λ_n=O(log n), then prove ||f−I_nf||∞≤(1+Λ_n)E_n(f). Use existing Weierstrass density only to show best polynomial errors tend to zero; do not infer that arbitrary-node interpolation converges. Barycentric evaluation is an algorithmic interface, not a stability theorem.

Proof route: Reduce the Chebyshev cardinal sum to the relevant trigonometric sum and establish the logarithmic estimate locally; then use I_np=p for p∈P_n and take the infimum. Record the node family, boundary convention, norm, and source-specific hypotheses. Equispaced divergence is a counterexample, not a conflict with Weierstrass.

Binding contract completion: Specify n+1 Chebyshev roots or n+1 Lobatto nodes, with n=0 treated separately for Lobatto. Prove Λ_n≤C log(n+1)+C′; transfer a concrete best-approximation rate rather than infer convergence from E_n→0 alone, since log(n)E_n need not tend to zero. Complex Runge approximation is optional context, not a premise for the real Runge interpolation example.

label: NA-12
title: Composite quadrature rules
description:
Define uniform-panel midpoint, trapezoid, and composite Simpson algorithms. For f∈C²[a,b] and h=(b−a)/n, prove midpoint error ≤(b−a)h²||f''||∞/24 and trapezoid error ≤(b−a)h²||f''||∞/12. For even n and f∈C⁴[a,b], prove composite Simpson error ≤(b−a)h⁴||f⁽⁴⁾||∞/180 and exactness through cubic degree. Keep smoothness and panel-count hypotheses in every claim.

Proof route: Integrate the panelwise Taylor remainder for midpoint, the piecewise-linear interpolation error for trapezoid, and the fourth-order Peano/Taylor remainder for Simpson; explicitly show the cubic cancellation. Prove procedure definitions separately from error estimates.

Binding contract completion: Inputs are a<b, finite callable f and integer n≥1 (even n≥2 for Simpson); outputs are the stated finite weighted sums with h=(b−a)/n. Midpoint uses interior midpoints, trapezoid half endpoint weights, Simpson weights 1,4,2,…,4,1 times h/3. Each error proof specifies real scalar f and the relevant uniform derivative norm. Rounded quadrature has a separate summation error.

label: NA-13
title: Gaussian quadrature
description:
For positive dμ=w(x)dx on [a,b], finite moments through degree 2m for the remainder integral (degree 2m−1 suffices for rule exactness), and a positive-definite polynomial inner product through degree m for the remainder branch, construct the monic orthogonal polynomial p_m. Prove it has m simple roots in (a,b); the m-node Gauss rule at those roots has positive weights and exactness through degree 2m−1. For f∈C^{2m}[a,b], prove the remainder f^{(2m)}(ξ)/(2m)! ∫p_m²dμ. Tensor products preserve coordinatewise exactness but cost exponentially in dimension.

Proof route: Use Gram–Schmidt; prove root count by sign changes; divide q=p_mr+s and use orthogonality for exactness; apply exactness to ℓ_i² for positive weights; use Hermite interpolation at double nodes and repeated Rolle for the remainder. Each intermediate theorem is an explicit local proof obligation. To retain the exactness-only degree-2m−1 moment variant, construct p_m from its m orthogonality equations using the degree-(m−1) positive moment matrix and nonzero density support; do not pretend a degree-m quadratic norm is defined without the degree-2m moment.

Binding contract completion: m≥1; μ is a finite positive measure w dx with positive-definite degree-m polynomial moment matrix. Node construction is mathematical until a finite root/isolation oracle or root algorithm is supplied. Solve weights by cardinal integrals. Prove repeated-zero Rolle/Hermite remainder and a weighted mean-value theorem to obtain one ξ; exactness and positivity do not supply a computed-node/weight stability result.

title: Gaussian quadrature — Examples

label: NA-14
title: Adaptive quadrature and error indicators
description:
Define a terminating adaptive Simpson procedure with a finite depth/panel cap, nested estimates, accept/reject rule, and explicit “cap reached” output. Define embedded-rule differences as indicators only. Do not report the requested tolerance as a certified true-error bound. A certificate theorem is optional and remains outside the promised scope until an a-posteriori remainder bound, stability propagation, regularity, and controlled-arithmetic premise are each supplied.

Proof route: Prove termination from the finite cap and correctness of returned arithmetic outputs, not accuracy from the indicator. Any later certificate must bound each accepted panel’s true defect and propagate defects with the integral/ODE stability operator, including roundoff. Preserve the source’s counterexample to estimator reliability.

Binding contract completion: Inputs a<b, ε>0, finite depth D and finite-evaluation f. Compare child Simpson sum S₂ with parent S using |S₂−S|/15; accept the chosen corrected or uncorrected estimate explicitly. On rejection halve the interval and tolerance, unless D is reached; then return the estimate with cap status. Nonfinite evaluations or unrepresentable midpoints return failure. A depth-D binary tree has at most 2^(D+1)−1 nodes; this proves termination, not accuracy.

label: NA-15
title: Runge–Kutta methods and order
description:
Define explicit Runge–Kutta tableaux and their one-step maps. Derive the method-specific order conditions for Euler, explicit midpoint, and the classical fourth-order method. Define the stability function R(z) by applying the method to y'=λy. Keep order, stability region, and stiffness separate. The generic local-defect and fixed-step global-error contracts remain P-NUM-ODE-01/02; this pair supplies the concrete tableau/order-condition interface, not duplicate generic error claims.

Proof route: Expand the exact flow and the three selected stage updates by multivariable Taylor, match the rooted-tree coefficients through each stated order, and identify the method-specific local order conditions. P-NUM-ODE-01 owns an abstract defect/stability theorem whose hypotheses are instantiated by these conditions, without any logical edge from that pre-category supplier back to NA-15; this pair states no separate fixed-interval error theorem. Prove the stability function by algebra on the scalar test equation. A method name or observed order plot does not prove the method-specific conditions.

Binding contract completion: Explicit tableaux have a_ij=0 for j≥i; on N fixed steps compute stages in increasing i and update y+hΣb_i k_i. All stage points must remain in the declared smooth tube. Nonautonomous expansions use augmented (t,y), not the autonomous formula unchanged. Classical RK4 local O(h⁵) requires the stated four-flow-derivative/Taylor bounds; no P-NUM→NA-15→P-NUM cycle.

label: NA-16
title: Linear multistep methods and Dahlquist equivalence
description:
Define a fixed-step k-step recurrence, generating polynomials ρ and σ, local truncation error from inserting the exact solution, consistency conditions ρ(1)=0 and ρ'(1)=σ(1), and order p. Define the root condition as roots in |ζ|≤1 with simple unit-modulus roots; repeated roots strictly inside are permitted. Prove equal-step convergence order p from consistency, root condition, O(h^p) starting values, a fixed solution tube, and a well-defined selected implicit branch. Prove the converse in the stated Dahlquist equivalence class.

Proof route: Complete the repeated-root proof; rewrite the recurrence as a companion system; prove uniformly bounded powers from the root condition; use variation of constants to propagate O(h^{p+1}) residuals over O(h^-1) steps. For necessity, use the consistency defect and unstable/parasitic homogeneous modes. Do not use one-step discrete Grönwall as a substitute for the root condition, and do not extend the equal-step proof to variable steps without new hypotheses.

Binding contract completion: Normalize α_k≠0; declare k, all coefficients, starting k values and N steps. Implicit solves have a specified branch and a proved small-step uniqueness condition; no undefined root selection. A full Jordan/companion-power lemma handles repeated interior roots. Necessity concerns convergence for every admissible equation and consistent start family, not a single test problem or favorable start.

label: NA-17
title: Stability regions and stiff equations
description:
Define R(z) and the one-step absolute-stability region for y'=λy; define multistep stability by roots of ρ(ζ)−zσ(ζ). Define A-stability as inclusion of the closed left half-plane and L-stability, for a rational one-step function, as A-stability plus decay R(z)→0 at infinity in that half-plane. Prove backward Euler is A- and L-stable, while trapezoidal is A-stable but not L-stable. Stability is a scalar test-equation property, not an accuracy theorem or universal definition of stiffness.

Proof route: Compute the stability functions and their regions; for multistep methods apply the root condition at each z and keep unit-root simplicity. Prove the limiting condition separately from half-plane inclusion. Treat stiff behavior as an application-dependent reason for implicit stepping, not as an unproved scalar classification.

Binding contract completion: Absolute one-step stability means |R(z)|≤1 with R defined (no pole). For multistep methods demand all roots |ζ|≤1 with simple unit roots and nonvanishing leading coefficient at that z. If terminology uses strict decay instead, the imaginary-axis boundary is treated separately; the adopted A-stability convention uses boundedness on the closed left half-plane.

label: NA-18
title: Adaptive ODE solvers and error estimation
description:
Define an embedded Runge–Kutta pair, local difference estimator, step acceptance/rejection, safety factor, norm scaling, and minimum/maximum step rules as an algorithm with finite stopping safeguards. State the asymptotic estimate E(h)≈Ch^{p+1} and controller exponent only as a model used to choose a step. Do not claim a global adaptive error certificate or infer stiffness from an estimator.

Proof route: Specify every branch and demonstrate algorithm termination under a finite step/depth budget. The estimator’s exponent follows only when its leading defect coefficient is present and the asymptotic regime holds. A global adaptive theorem requires estimator reliability, mesh-ratio regularity, and defect propagation; none is supplied here.

Binding contract completion: Supply pair orders, p, norm scaling atol_i+rtol_i max(|y_i|,|y_i,new|)>0, safety factor and bounded step multipliers. Zero estimated defect chooses the maximum multiplier. Final steps clip to T, failed rejection at h_min or floating t+h=t returns failure, and every trial consumes the finite budget. Successful completion is a status, not a global tolerance theorem.

label: NA-19
title: Linear scheme stability and Lax equivalence
description:
Define consistency, convergence, and finite-time stability for a well-posed linear IVP on one common Banach space, with bounded step operators S_k and a mesh function h(k). State Lax–Richtmyer only in that same-norm setting: for a consistent approximation to the declared well-posed problem, convergence iff uniform finite-time stability. State explicitly that Trefethen’s read chapter marks the proof unwritten; this row requires a complete local proof and a concrete mesh-to-common-space interface.

Proof route: For stability→convergence, write the Duhamel error sum on a smooth dense class, bound propagators uniformly, and then extend by density and continuous dependence. For convergence→stability, show pointwise boundedness of the operator family on each compact time interval and apply the published Banach–Steinhaus theorem. For mesh-dependent spaces, define reconstruction/projection and prove norm comparisons; do not silently apply the common-space theorem. A spectral-radius or CFL check alone is not the stability premise.

Binding contract completion: Supply a strongly continuous well-posed solution semigroup E(t), a dense invariant consistency core and bounds uniform for 0≤j k≤T. Local defects are o(k) uniformly on exact core trajectories; convergence means sup_(j k≤T)||S_k^j x−E(jk)x||→0 for every x. This uniform mode gives pointwise boundedness for UBP/DC; arbitrary pointwise-in-time convergence is insufficient. Projection/reconstruction variants prove their own density and norm bounds.

title: Linear scheme stability and Lax equivalence — Examples

label: NA-20
